prompt:
Build a three-dimensional Simscape Multibody handling mechanism that transfers one free six-degree-of-freedom box from a moving input conveyor, through active gripper capture and transport, onto an orthogonal moving output conveyor. Both conveyor interfaces must use finite-compliance normal collision and tangential stick-slip friction with explicit contact separation or penetration. The gripper must physically capture, retain, move, and release the box; do not replace the box with a prescribed pose, replayed trajectory, or signal-only state machine. This task contains one transferred box and does not require stacking.

Read InputBeltSpeedScale, OutputBeltSpeedScale, BeltKineticFrictionScale, BeltStaticFrictionScale, and PayloadDensityScale from the MATLAB base workspace. Apply them to the actual belt motion, belt contact laws, and payload inertia while supporting the declared ranges. The internal command schedule, contact implementation, and gripper mechanism are not prescribed.

InputBeltSpeedScale and OutputBeltSpeedScale are real unitless scalars in [0.85, 1.1]; BeltKineticFrictionScale and BeltStaticFrictionScale are real unitless scalars in [0.8, 1.2]; and PayloadDensityScale is a real unitless scalar in [0.8, 1.25].

Run for 30 s and complete the physical sequence input-belt transport, gripper pickup and retention, cross-belt transfer, release, and output-belt transport. Keep all states and forces finite, bound contact penetration, and make normal and tangential forces act only through their corresponding physical contacts.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named box_state, command_state, input_contact, and output_contact. box_state has 6 channels in this order: x, y, z (m), then vx, vy, vz (m/s). command_state has 6 channels in this order: gripper-finger translation (m), gripper rotation (rad), gripper vertical translation (m), gripper post-rotation (rad), output-belt speed (m/s), and input-belt speed (m/s). input_contact and output_contact each have 8 channels in this order: separation (m), normal relative velocity (m/s), normal force (N), tangential x and y velocity (m/s), friction-force magnitude (N), and friction-force x and y components (N). Save the completed model as cand_XMECH07.slx in the submission directory and keep its latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XMECH07.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
